criteria: low hallucination, no repetition, no truncation

qwen2-7b-1ep.headline: Undertrained baseline: sometimes useful, but brittle and prone to invalid JSON or runaway output.

qwen2-7b-5ep.headline: Best value adapter: strong structure and practical SOC answers, but weaker on subtle Linux/systemd and process-injection details.

qwen3-30b-1ep.headline: High ceiling after one epoch, but one catastrophic repetition/truncation failure makes it less dependable than the 7B 5-epoch run.

qwen3-30b-5ep.headline: Clear winner: best reasoning quality, best format reliability, strongest technical depth, and lowest average latency in this eval.

case_scores.topic: developer workstation pull-request preview, OAuth app abuse, postinstall execution
case_scores.judge_note: The 30B 5-epoch output best tied the browser-origin file write, npm/postinstall behavior, forked PR, and OAuth scope grant into a coherent supply-chain/CI abuse hypothesis. Qwen2 1-epoch produced invalid answer JSON.

The best answers recognized the specific sudoers env_keep abuse path and explained why an unmodified app binary is not exculpatory. The weaker answers used fuzzier technique mapping or implied the service binary itself was the main execution target.

case_scores.topic: rundll32 remote-share DLL load from remote service session
case_scores.judge_note: The 30B 5-epoch run gave a clean lateral-movement/proxy-execution answer. The 30B 1-epoch run failed catastrophically with repetitive text and no closing tags.

case_scores.topic: kernel KTIMER/KDPC execution from non-paged pool
case_scores.judge_note: The 30B models understood why DPC/timer execution does not create user-mode threads. The 5-epoch model was tighter and more defender-actionable.
All non-1ep-7B models recognized Drupalgeddon-style RCE, webshell placement, payload fetch, and admin persistence. Qwen2 1-epoch went into a malformed, repetitive source-metadata spiral.

case_scores.topic: regini registry permission and ImagePath tampering
case_scores.judge_note: The 30B 5-epoch answer best separated legitimate policy work from malicious script-host-to-regini abuse by combining parentage, path, target keys, and change context.

case_scores.topic: malicious npm package on macOS developer workstation
case_scores.judge_note: The 30B 5-epoch output was strongest at explaining package-name deception, fork delivery, credential exfiltration, and immediate endpoint/cloud hunts.
The 30B 5-epoch answer was the clearest on duplicate section handles, image-backed hash drift, missing private RX allocation, and what the detector should compare.

case_scores.topic: Linux archived systemd journal recovery and remote directory meaning
case_scores.judge_note: The 30B 5-epoch answer correctly named journalctl --file and interpreted remote/ as journal upload/forwarding context. Both 7B answers gave misleading statements about local journal clearing or attacker staging.

case_scores.topic: incident-response lifecycle feedback after Linux web compromise
case_scores.judge_note: The 30B 1-epoch answer gave the best complete IR lifecycle feedback. The 30B 5-epoch answer was concise but hallucinated 'case study' framing and included shaky technique labeling.

bottom_line: The 30B 5-epoch model is the best fine-tuned model in this test. The 7B 5-epoch model is the best cost/performance result. The 30B 1-epoch model has strong reasoning when it behaves, but one severe runaway failure makes it risky. The 7B 1-epoch model is not reliable enough for endpoint investigator use.
